  "edges": [
    {
      "fromKey": "n-uk8heo",
      "toKey": "n-1x05929",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The work package cover shows the temporary instruction attachment field was blank (condition). A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released. The absence of an attached approved temporary instruction at issue time means the crew did not have documented authorization for any changed arrangement, leaving them reliant on potentially outdated or incomplete information.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": ["eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1","b678a928-a8d2-472d-bc03-2e1a3dc411e6#1"],
      "claimIds": ["claim-1p43v5g", "finding-nk53l1"],
      "counterfactual": "If the temporary instruction attachment field had contained an approved document at issue time, it would have provided documented evidence that a changed arrangement was authorized and distributed to the crew.",
      "competingExplanation": "The blank field could be due to administrative oversight rather than absence of any change; however, without documentation, the barrier (authorized knowledge) is functionally absent regardless of intent.",
      "evidenceGap": "Whether an unrecorded service-routing change actually occurred in reality versus whether it was simply not documented."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-14tzgyz",
      "toKey": "n-1wlpxtv",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The point register maps AL-44 to receiving-header pressure P-R, not compressor trip contact. The daily briefing attendance sheet lists U-A and U-B but contains no valve-by-valve content. This lack of specific coordination information in the briefing means crew members were not explicitly informed about individual valve states or routing changes during preparation.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": ["da0260c0-7d49-43e8-b074-da2a14c7d59c#1","7e69d300-c57e-40a8-bb37-35a61073ff33#1"],
      "claimIds": ["finding-nk53l1", "claim-1ado6d5"],
      "counterfactual": "If the daily briefing had included valve-by-valve content, crew members would have received explicit information about current conditions and any changes.",
      "competingExplanation": "The lack of detailed briefing might be standard procedure; however, in this case where a service-routing change could exist, such detail becomes critical for safety.",
      "evidenceGap": "Whether the absence of valve-by-valve content was intentional or due to oversight."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-18qtamm",
      "toKey": "n-1x05929",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution requirements for changed arrangements. The work package cover indicates the temporary instruction attachment field was blank at issue time, meaning no approved documentation accompanied the crew.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": ["0ff450fe-49da-4c67-8b42-35449fdad35c#1","eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1"],
      "claimIds": ["finding-nk53l1", "claim-1p43v5g"],
      "counterfactual": "If draft preparation had been followed by proper distribution (revision or approved temporary instruction), the crew would have received documented information about any changes.",
      "competingExplanation": "The requirement might not apply if no service-routing change occurred; however, without evidence to confirm this, we must assume potential hazard exists until proven otherwise.",
      "evidenceGap": "Whether a service-routing change actually existed that required distribution."
    }
  ],
  "decision": {
    "summary": "The investigation identifies three supported causal links: (1) blank temporary instruction attachment field combined with scheduling-only status means boundary not released; (2) lack of valve-by-valve briefing content prevents crew from knowing specific conditions; and (3) draft preparation without approved distribution fails to meet requirements. These create a chain where undocumented or undistributed changes could lead to hazard scenarios during maintenance.",
    "evidenceUsed": ["eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1", "b678a928-a8d2-472d-bc03-2e1a3dc411e6#1", "da0260c0-7d49-43e8-b074-da2a14c7d59c#1", "7e69d300-c57e-40a8-bb37-35a61073ff33#1"],
    "unknowns": ["Whether an unrecorded service-routing change actually occurred versus simply not being documented.", "Whether the lack of valve-by-valve briefing was intentional or due to oversight."],
    "alternatives": ["The interruption might have originated from a different cause unrelated to documentation gaps, such as equipment failure upstream.", "The crew may have had informal knowledge that wasn't captured in records but still failed to act appropriately."],
    "confidence": 0.75
  },"evidenceRequests":[

]
}
